content:
OpenAI is rolling out a new way for ChatGPT and Codex to learn and remember how you use your Mac, even when that activity happens outside the apps themselves.

Computer History for ChatGPT is an upgraded replacement for the existing Chronicle research preview in Codex

The new Computer History feature builds a searchable timeline of activity from selected apps and websites.

OpenAI announced Computer History in its Thursday desktop app release notes. The feature is off by default and must be opted into by users, giving them control over which sources are included in the record.

The update comes exactly one month after Codex moved into the ChatGPT desktop app, and hot on the heels of OpenAI’s experimental Chronicle feature earlier in the year.

OpenAI describes Computer History as the effective replacement for the Chronicle research preview, but stresses that it is a rebuilt system, not simply a rename.

Chronicle relied on screenshots. Computer History instead records interaction events detected through macOS accessibility, including clicks, typing, keyboard shortcuts, and switching between different apps.

Here’s how OpenAI describes the new feature:

Computer History is an opt-in feature in the ChatGPT macOS desktop app that turns activity across apps and websites into memories and a timeline, available to both ChatGPT and Codex. Users can choose which apps and websites are included in the record, pause collection at any time, and view or delete history. Computer History is currently available to ChatGPT Pro, Business, and Enterprise users. Admins on Business and Enterprise plans must first enable access before workspace members can turn the feature on. The EEA, Switzerland, and the UK are not included in the initial rollout.

OpenAI also explains how eligible users can enable the opt-in Computer History feature:

Users will be able to ask what they were doing before bed, find a recently viewed document, or generate a summary of their day’s work. ChatGPT may also suggest turning repetitive workflows into skills or automations.

Computer History and privacy

OpenAI says ChatGPT’s Computer History feature does not capture screenshots, screen recordings, microphone input, or system audio. Anonymous browsing activity is also excluded.

Users can view timeline entries in settings, reveal individual memory files in Finder, delete specific items, or clear activity from the past 10 minutes, hour, day, or all time.

Computer History temporarily stores interaction events on your Mac for up to 48 hours. OpenAI says these events are processed on its servers to generate the relevant memories, but are not retained afterwards and are not used for training. The final plain-text memory files are stored locally until the user deletes them.

OpenAI also warns that the Computer History feature may increase the risk of prompt injection because of malicious content in apps or websites. The company recommends pausing collection when communicating with others without their explicit consent, and excluding apps that handle sensitive information.
